result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_gnc_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a growing network with copying (GNC): each new node links to a random node and to ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11398-L11490){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_gnc_graph( n, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} everything it links to. ![Growing network with copying](/assets/graphs/add-gnc-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three growing networks with copying on 4, 5, and 6 nodes, placed on a ring in arrival order. Each new node links to a random existing node and also copies all of that node's arcs, so arcs pile onto the earliest nodes: the first node receives 3, 4, and 5 arcs, and the graphs have 4, 7, and 11 arcs in all." width="100%"} Adds nodes one at a time. Each new node picks an existing node uniformly at random and links to it and to every node it links to. Since those links were copied the same way, a node's out-neighbors are exactly the nodes on the path from it back to the first node in the underlying random tree. The result is a directed acyclic graph that is transitively closed: whenever `a -> b -> c`, also `a -> c`. It models a paper that cites another along with that one's references. The model is due to Krapivsky and Redner; the process follows NetworkX's `gnc_graph()`. Each edge points from the new node to an older one. In an undirected graph the same edges are added without their direction. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. GNC graphs are useful for: - modeling citation networks in which references are copied - random transitively closed DAGs, e.g. as partial orders - comparing against `add_gnr_graph()`, which copies a single link instead of all of them ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Copying links makes the graph much denser than a tree: ::: {#bb9119a3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_gnc_graph(n=50, seed=2) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 137) ``` ::: ::: Every node's successors include all of its successors' successors: ::: {#581e07ef .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} all( set(graph.get_successors(w)) <= set(graph.get_successors(v)) for v in graph.get_node_ids() for w in graph.get_successors(v) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
